title: Monoclonal Antibodies Directed Against Amyloid for the Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease (AD)
service: Anti-amyloid monoclonal antibody for Alzheimer's disease

criteria.text: Clinical diagnosis of MCI due to AD or mild AD dementia
criteria.span: for patients who have a clinical diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to AD or mild AD dementia
both with confirmed presence of amyloid beta pathology consistent with AD

criteria.text: Traditional-approval drugs: only in CMS-approved prospective comparative studies (registry allowed)
criteria.span: Monoclonal antibodies directed against amyloid that are approved by the FDA for the treatment of AD based upon evidence of efficacy from a direct measure of clinical benefit may be covered in CMS-approved prospective comparative studies

criteria.text: Accelerated-approval (surrogate endpoint) drugs: only in an RCT under an IND
criteria.span: based upon evidence of efficacy from a change in a surrogate endpoint (e.g., amyloid reduction) considered as reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit may be covered in a randomized controlled trial conducted under an investigational new drug (IND) application

Monoclonal antibodies directed against amyloid indicated for the treatment of AD are covered when furnished according to the FDA approved indication in National Institutes of Health (NIH)-supported trials

criteria.text: Non-covered outside FDA RCTs, CMS-approved studies, or NIH-supported studies
criteria.span: provided outside of an FDAapproved randomized controlled trial, CMS-approved studies, or studies supported by the NIH, are nationally non-covered

notes: Traditional approval (direct clinical benefit) -> CMS-approved prospective comparative study/registry; accelerated approval (surrogate) -> RCT under IND only; NIH-supported trials also covered.
